name: Curve Appeal: Curved vs Angular Shapes
description: Faithful replication of the two image-rating tasks in Cotter, Silvia, Bertamini, Palumbo & Vartanian (2017), "Curve Appeal: Exploring Individual Differences in Preference for Curved Versus Angular Objects", i-Perception 8(2). Part 1: 24 black-and-white irregular polygons, angular or curved (smoothed with a cubic spline), with 10, 18 or 26 vertices and two radius ranges, in two sets. Part 2: the 18 arrays of the Preference for Balance Test (Wilson & Chatterjee 2005): 9 of circles and 9 of hexagons, at low, medium and high imbalance. Images appear in random order and can be viewed as long as wished (at least 2 s). After each, participants rate on 1–7 scales how PLEASANT and how INTERESTING the image is, and for polygons also how COMPLEX it is, in that fixed order. Viewing time is recorded. Instructions follow the authors' MediaLab script. Analysis as in the paper: curved vs angular means per participant, and multilevel models with curvature as a within-person factor. Stimuli: the authors' image files from OSF (osf.io/vrjyp). Credit: doi:10.1177/2041669517693023. The template is removed if the authors object. Differences from the original study: (1) Online instead of a lab with MediaLab; the rating questions appear on a separate screen after the image, as in the original. (2) The individual-difference measures (Aesthetic Fluency Scale, HEXACO-100, NEO-FFI, BFAS Openness/Intellect, Need for Cognition, Types of Intuition Scale) are not included; several are licensed instruments and the paper does not print the items. Only age, gender and an arts major/minor question are asked. (3) The infrequency (attention-check) scale used to exclude inattentive participants is not included. (4) The Part 2 instructions adapt the Part 1 wording, because the original script text for that part could not be read from the OSF files.

elements.name: polygon_rating
elements.title: Irregular polygons: pleasantness, interest and complexity
elements.description: 24 black-and-white irregular polygons (Bertamini et al. 2016; Palumbo & Bertamini 2016): angular ('polygon') vs curved ('smooth') versions × 10/18/26 vertices × 2 radius ranges (40/60) × 2 sets (a, i). Shown in random order, each for as long as the participant wishes (at least 2 s), then rated 1–7 on pleasantness, interest and complexity in that fixed order. Value: {pleasant, interesting, complex, view_ms}. File names code the factors: <set>_<polygon|smooth>_<vertices>_<range>.jpg. Analysis as in the paper: multilevel models of ratings with curvature (within) and individual differences (between).

elements.name: balance_rating
elements.title: Preference for Balance Test: circles and hexagons
elements.description: Preference for Balance Test (Wilson & Chatterjee 2005): 18 arrays, 9 of circles (curved) and 9 of hexagons (angular); 3 images at each of 3 levels of imbalance (file numbers 0x low, 2x medium, 4x high). Random order, viewed as long as wished (at least 2 s), then rated 1–7 on pleasantness and interest. Value: {pleasant, interesting, view_ms}.
